title: Adjacency-diametrical matrix of a graph
summary: The adjacency-diametrical matrix (AD matrix) of a connected graph $G$ with diameter $d$, denoted by $AD(G)$, is the matrix indexed by the vertices of $G$ in which the $(i,j)$-entry of $AD(G)$ is $1$ if $d_G(v_i,v_j)=1$, is $d$ if $d_G(v_i,v_j)=d$, and $0$ otherwise, where $d_G(v_i,v_j)$ denotes the distance between the vertices $v_i$ and $v_j$ in $G$. We determine the spectrum of the AD matrix for paths, cycles, and double star graphs and obtain its determinant for a connected graph.
